blocks.prompt: 7. A train moving at 54 km/h is accelerated uniformly to 90 km/h in 20 s. Find the acceleration and the distance covered in this time.
blocks.explanation:
Uniform acceleration, so the equations of motion apply.
Given: u = 54 km/h, v = 90 km/h, t = 20 s. To find: a and the distance.
Plan: change both speeds to m/s, then v = u + at, then x = ut + at^2/2.
steps:
Given: \(u = 54\) km/h, \(v = 90\) km/h, \(t = 20\) s.
To find: the acceleration \(a\) and the distance \(x\).
Method: equations of motion with constant acceleration (7.1.6). The time is in seconds, so the speeds must be in m/s.

Change the speeds to m/s
\[u = 54 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 15\text{ m/s}\]
\[v = 90 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 25\text{ m/s}\]
Why: 1 km/h = 1000 m / 3600 s = 5/18 m/s.

Acceleration from \(v = u + at\)
\[25 = 15 + a(20)\]
\[20a = 10 \Rightarrow a = 0.5\text{ m/s}^2\]
Why: only a is unknown in this equation.

Distance from \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\)
\[x = 15(20) + \tfrac{1}{2}(0.5)(20)^2\]
\[= 300 + 100 = 400\text{ m}\]
Why: u, a and t are now known; the train moves in one direction, so this is the distance.

Check with \(2ax = v^2 - u^2\)
\[2(0.5)(400) = 400\]
\[25^2 - 15^2 = 625 - 225 = 400 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the third equation agrees. The area of the trapezium under the velocity-time graph is also \(\frac{1}{2}(15 + 25)(20) = 400\).
